tag and a mismatched pair is undetectable downstream.

Observed 2026-08-25 during Session G: gas-static-v1.3.0 and gas-deploy-v1.3.0 were created locally
and pushed together with a single `git push --tags`. GitHub created NO workflow run for either tag
ref — confirmed against the Actions API, which shows runs for the master push at 06:16 and for
gas-static-v1.3.1 (pushed alone at 06:18) but nothing for the two v1.3.0 tags. The guard is
therefore skippable by accident: push two tags at once and it never fires.

This is GitHub behaviour, not a workflow bug — runs are suppressed when multiple refs arrive in one
push. The guard's value is in exactly the case it silently skipped.

title: Bound script getService().getUrl() returns bound script deployment, not webapp deployment
description:
When a Google Apps Script project has both a bound script (attached to a spreadsheet) and a web app enabled:

**Problem:** Calling ScriptApp.getService().getUrl() from bound script code returns the deployment ID of the bound script, NOT the webapp's deployment ID. If the bound script and webapp are running under different deployments (e.g., due to separate deploy cycles or stale execution contexts), the URLs will not match.

**Impact:** Code that relies on ScriptApp.getService().getUrl() to identify the current webapp endpoint will get the wrong URL. In F3Go30, this caused signup short URLs to be created/reused pointing to a stale webapp deployment while the actual current webapp was running under a different deployment ID.

**Solution:** Explicitly store the webapp's URL as a Script Property when the webapp runs (e.g., via an admin action like setWebappUrl). Bound script code should read this Script Property instead of calling getService().getUrl().

**Design Note:** This is a critical distinction for any GAS project with both bound and webapp components. Do not assume getService().getUrl() returns the canonical webapp URL — it returns the deployment URL of whatever context the code is running in.

title: Fold in clasp-auth, webapp-testing, and TEST/PROD-data-isolation lessons from F3Go30 into best-practices/
description:
## Source

F3Go30 (`/mnt/c/dev/F3Go30`), session 2026-06-24 implementing the HC signup webapp
(`docs/signup-webapp-requirements.md`, tracked as F3Go30-bmm2) and fixing a clasp credential
mixup. See `/mnt/c/dev/F3Go30/work-log.md` entry `## 2026-06-24 05:50:00` for full session
narrative; `bd memories` in F3Go30 has the raw facts (`clasp-config-auth-env-var`,
`test-app-shares-live-template-spreadsheet`).

## Purpose

Several non-obvious, real (not theoretical) lessons came out of this session that apply beyond
F3Go30. Update the relevant `best-practices/` folders so the next GAS project doesn't re-learn
them the hard way.

## Items to fold in, by existing folder

### `gas-deployment/` and `gas-cm-and-deployment/`

**clasp's actual auth env var is `clasp_config_auth` (lower-case, exact match), not
`CLASP_CONFIG`.** Verified by grepping the installed `@google/clasp@3.3.0` source directly:
`commands/program.js` registers `new Option('-A, --auth <file>', ...).env('clasp_config_auth')`
as a **global** option, applying to every subcommand (`login`, `push`, `deploy`, `status`,
`run`, `deployments`, ...) — not just `login`. Commander does an exact-case
`option.envVar in process.env` lookup. `CLASP_CONFIG` is not registered anywhere in clasp's
source; setting it is a silent no-op.

This matters a lot for any project (like F3Go30, or future multi-account setups) that needs to
switch between multiple Google account credentials via named `.clasprc-*.json` files — neither
existing doc currently says how to point clasp at a non-default credential file. Both should
gain a section like:

```bash
# Authenticate (creates/refreshes the credential file)
clasp_config_auth=~/.clasprc-myproject.json clasp login

# Every other clasp command reads the same var
clasp_config_auth=~/.clasprc-myproject.json clasp push -f
clasp_config_auth=~/.clasprc-myproject.json clasp deploy --deploymentId <id>
```

**Also add a verification step** — before trusting a named credential file (e.g. after copying
one between projects, or after a long gap), confirm its actual identity rather than trusting the
filename:

```bash
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(jq -r '.tokens.default.access_token' ~/.clasprc-myproject.json)
curl -s "https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v2/userinfo?access_token=$ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

This caught a real incident in F3Go30: `~/.clasprc-f3go30.json` had drifted to an unrelated
personal Google Workspace account, and every clasp command using `CLASP_CONFIG` had been
silently falling back to the default `~/.clasprc.json` the whole time — masking the problem for
an entire session, because the wrong credential still happened to have project access.

**F3Go30's pattern for project-local credential paths:** a `claspAuth` field in
`local.settings.json` (gitignored), read by the deploy script and expanded (`~` → `os.homedir()`)
before being passed via `clasp_config_auth` in the child process `env`. Worth adding as the
canonical multi-credential pattern if `gas-cm-and-deployment/manage-deployments.js` doesn't
already have one.

**`gas-deployment/`'s TEST/PROD architecture should add a Constraints/Trade-offs bullet:**
*"Verify what data your TEST deployment's bound spreadsheet/script project actually is before
relying on it for write-path testing — a 'TEST' deployment name does not imply isolated test
data. It may be the same script project (and therefore the same Spreadsheet container) used for
live/PROD data, especially in single-script-project setups where TEST/PROD differ only by which
spreadsheet is opened at runtime via an ID looked up from config."* This was a real near-miss in
F3Go30: `TEST_APP` is a named deployment on the **Template** script project, and the webapp's own
business logic resolves "current month" to whichever tracker is genuinely live right now — a
live-write test against "current" wrote a throwaway row into the actual in-use spreadsheet.
Caught and cleaned up, but avoidable with a documented warning.

### `gas-cm-and-deployment/` (lighter-weight version stamping)

F3Go30 added a simpler alternative to the full pattern documented there: every `deploy()` call
auto-bumps `package.json`'s **patch** version (no git commit/tag, just the file), unless a
`--skip-bump` flag is passed (used by `release:patch/minor/major`, which already bump via
`npm version`). This avoids a git commit on every test/month deploy while still guaranteeing each
pushed/deployed version is unique and distinguishable in the stamped `version.js`. Worth noting
as a "Lighter-weight alternative" callout for projects that don't want git history noise from
every test deploy.

### `google-sheet-verification/`

Confirm the unauthenticated xlsx-export trick also works from plain shell (`curl -sL`), not just
Python `requests` — useful for a quick manual check without writing a script:

```bash
curl -sL "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<ID>/export?format=xlsx" -o sheet.xlsx
```

Add the same TEST/PROD data-isolation caution as above to this doc's Constraints table — the xlsx
export technique makes it *easy* to verify sheet content, which is exactly when a write-path test
against a shared live spreadsheet feels safe but isn't.

### New: testing a deployed Web App's `doPost`/`doGet` via curl (no existing home — candidate
new folder `gas-webapp-curl-testing/`, or fold into `gas-acceptance-testing/` since it already
covers POSTing actions to `/exec`)

**curl gotcha, not yet documented anywhere:** Google's Web App `/exec` endpoint responds to both
GET and POST with a 302 redirect to a GET-only `script.googleusercontent.com/macros/echo`
endpoint. Passing an explicit `-X POST` to curl pins that method through the redirect (curl's
documented behavior when `-X` is set explicitly), causing the *second* request to hit the
GET-only echo endpoint as a POST — Google's frontend returns a generic, misleading
"Page Not Found" HTML page (it's actually a 405, but curl without `-v` won't show that). Python's
`requests` library does not have this problem (it downgrades POST→GET on 302 by default, same as
curl's own *default* behavior) — this only bites people who explicitly pass `-X POST` out of habit
or for clarity.

```bash
# Wrong — looks like a 404, is actually a 405 from the redirect target
curl -s -X POST "$EXEC_URL" --data-raw '{"action":"ping"}'

# Right — let --data imply POST, omit -X, always pass -L
curl -s -L "$EXEC_URL" --data-raw '{"action":"ping"}' -H "Content-Type: text/plain"
```

This is a small, sharp, easy-to-rediscover-the-hard-way gotcha — worth a short, prominent note
wherever curl-based manual testing of a GAS Web App is documented.

### New / unclear home: Claude-design mockup export format is not GAS-deployable as-is

If a UI mockup is produced via the "Claude design" tool (artifact export as `.dc.html` +
`support.js`), the exported format is a proprietary preview-tool runtime requiring
`window.React`/`window.ReactDOM` as globals and a custom `x-dc`/`sc-if`/`sc-for` templating layer
— it is **not** a static, deployable artifact. GAS `HtmlService` only serves plain static files
with no build step, so the mockup must be manually ported to vanilla HTML/CSS/JS (or a
CDN-script-tag framework with zero build step) before it can back a `doGet`-served page. Worth a
short note if/when GAS-Core documents a UI-mockup-to-HtmlService workflow — no existing folder
covers this; lower priority than the items above since it's only relevant when that specific
design tool is used.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `gas-deployment/README.md` and/or `gas-cm-and-deployment/README.md` document
      `clasp_config_auth` as the real clasp auth env var (global, all subcommands), explicitly
      correct the `CLASP_CONFIG` misconception, and show the multi-credential-file pattern with
      the userinfo identity-verification step.
- [ ] `gas-deployment/README.md` gains a Constraints/Trade-offs bullet about verifying TEST
      deployments don't share live data with PROD.
- [ ] `google-sheet-verification/README.md` confirms the curl one-liner and adds the same
      shared-live-data caution.
- [ ] `gas-cm-and-deployment/README.md` documents the lighter-weight auto-patch-bump-per-deploy
      alternative (no git commit/tag) alongside the full `npm version` pattern.
- [ ] The curl `-X POST` redirect gotcha is documented somewhere discoverable (new folder or
      folded into `gas-acceptance-testing/`) — decide placement during implementation.
- [ ] Top-level `best-practices/README.md` index updated for any new/changed folder, with F3Go30
      added as a source where applicable (it's already listed for `gas-email-templating/`).

title: PUBLISHERS.md prose table and JSON ownership block can drift with nothing to notice

S4 built the publish ownership guard: PUBLISHERS.md carries a human folder->project->live-URL table AND a fenced JSON block, and gas-static reads the FIRST json fence. Two statements of the same fact in one file, and only one of them runs.

S4's handoff records this as a deliberate non-filing: 'Did not add a CI check that the prose table and the JSON block agree — the JSON is what runs; noted in ADR-0003 Harder rather than filed, since no consumer has drifted yet.' That reasoning was right at the time. Filing it now so the risk is visible somewhere a person looks, rather than only in an accepted ADR's Consequences section, which nobody re-reads.

Not urgent, and possibly never worth building: two host repos with four and one entries respectively. The trigger to act is a third host repo, or the first observed disagreement. What makes it worth a record: a drifted prose table misleads a human into publishing to a folder the JSON does not register, and the failure then looks like the guard being wrong rather than the doc being wrong.

Cheapest fix if taken: a test in packages/gas-static/test/ that parses both halves of a fixture PUBLISHERS.md and asserts they agree, plus a note in the package README telling host-repo maintainers to edit both.

### What's done (2026-06-19)
- **Created**: examples/demos/libsheets-basic/smoke.spec.js (one test: menu click → demo execution)

- Drives the real Sheets editor UI via Playwright (menu clicks, onOpen menu, sidebar)

- Asserts on visible side effect (sheet tabs created by demo) not just menu presence
- Per-library harness (libsheets-basic demo) — demonstrates single-lib Tier 3 workflow

### Blocker: Manual/headed testing required
Playwright requires:
1. **Network install**: `npm install @playwright/test` (sandboxed in this repo, cannot auto-run)
2. **Live Google auth**: User runs `npx playwright test --headed` once interactively → captures .auth/user.json
3. **Live Sheet URL**: `SHEET_URL=<bound sheet URL> npx playwright test`
4. **Headed browser**: Chrome must be visible (GAS editor nested iframes cannot be driven headless)

**Cannot be automated in CI** — this is the documented trade-off for Tier 3 (real UI coverage, manual/periodic gate).

   - Open the bound Sheet in browser (get URL from demo.config.json _execUrl or GAS editor)

2. **If selectors fail** (Google editor DOM changed):
   - Update selectors in smoke.spec.js (currently #docs-menubar, getByRole('menuitem'/'tab'))
   - Re-run manual test
   
3. **Expand Tier 3** (out of scope, post-MVP):
   - Add tests for libsheets-with-notifications (sidebar interaction)
   - Add tests for other library demos as they mature
   - Document periodic smoke-test CI job (manual trigger, not auto-gate)

**GAS-Core-2xf**: Sheet host needs one-time OAuth consent (user opens the GAS editor, authorizes SpreadsheetApp scope, saves). After that, both Tier 2 (doGet) and Tier 3 (UI) tests can run.
